stage2_results.local_context:
When you hear “space weapons,” it may sound like one kind of weapon. But the key to understanding this news is not to imagine what the weapons can do. It is to ask, “Where are they?” and check their address.

In September 2026, the U.S. Secretary of the Air Force said that the United States was deploying space-control weapons in orbit to protect the Joint Force from the actions of hostile parties. An official article by a U.S. government agency records this as the first statement to acknowledge the Space Force’s deployment of weapons. However, the weapons’ names, ability to attack, and targets were not made clear. All we know is that they are being deployed in orbit.

It is important not to mix this up with a missile launched from the ground to attack a satellite. In 2021, Russia fired a missile from the ground and destroyed a satellite. More than 1,500 pieces of debris could be tracked. That was a case of targeting space from the ground. This announcement is about deploying weapons in orbit. The difference is not only whether the target is in space; the weapons are in different places, too.
